commits.message:
Resume a chain-sync stream from its events, not the open answer's point

The sidecar's answer to cs_open settles a promise, while stream frames are
dispatched synchronously as each read chunk is parsed. When the answer and
the first events arrive in one chunk, the events are handled before the
open's continuation, which then overwrote the stream's last point with the
intersection and its tip with the answer's older one. A failure before the
next event made the stream resume from the intersection, so the sidecar
delivered the same blocks again: the consumer saw repeats, and the fake
sidecar test saw its consecutive-failure count reset (3 of the last 40
l1-node-transport CI runs on #814 failed this way).

The continuation now keeps a position and tip that events have already
set. The fake sidecar sends an open's answer and the events it releases in
one write, so its tests always take the coalesced path a busy client sees;
"records each failure a resuming stream reopens from" fails on every run
against the old continuation and passed 40 of 40 runs after the fix.

Hold the transition-trace fixture's deposit past a fresh history root's protection

On a fresh deployment the deposit-history root stays protected for the
deployment's protection window. The fixture built its deposit at once, so a
live journey started within that window failed with
EventHistoryPredecessorProtectedError. Earlier green runs used deployments
hours old.

The deposit build now goes through the bounded predecessor hold the history
staging already uses, on the chain's ledger clock. The hold moves to the
watcher's test support so both packages share it.

Deploy journey contracts with the Custom devnet's slot mapping

The published-workflow deployment helper applied the scripts and wrote the
manifest with Preprod's slot mapping whatever network it deployed to. On a
Custom devnet the watcher then refused every installed family with
l1_slot_config_mismatch, because the chain it reads anchors slot 0 at the
devnet's genesis, not at Preprod's Shelley start.

The helper now takes Preprod's constants for a Preprod deployment and, for a
Custom one, the mapping of the Lucid it deploys with, and uses that one value
for both the parameterised scripts and the manifest.

Lower the initialization emulator test's module-size cap to its new length

The fixture-staleness check shortened the file from 741 to 738 lines, and the size inventory refuses a cap above a file's length.

Fail the node suite when the watcher's initialization capture is stale

The initialization emulator test writes the watcher's captured
initialization transactions when MIDGARD_WRITE_WATCHER_INITIALIZATION_FIXTURE
is set, but nothing compared the capture's recorded blueprintSha256 with the
current build. A validator change left it stale silently, and its only
recipe (contrib test with the write flag) always ended in a failed receipt
because the fixture is one of midgard-node's own inputs.

The test now always checks the recorded hash against the current
blueprint, as da-deployment-fixture-generation already does, so the
channel gains a check and artifacts sync can regenerate it in a scratch
checkout.

Regression caught: a blueprint change without regenerating the capture now
fails "Test Midgard node" in CI, naming the sync command. It belongs in the
generating test because that is where the current hash is already computed.

Regenerate the watcher initialization fixture and re-copy the scan-plan pins

The tx-order script hash changed with the validity-bound decoding change, so
the watcher's recorded initialization still named the old tx-order address
and the follower capture dropped the forced order. The native-script-decoding
scan planner's execution pins still held the costs from before the body
decoders gained the bound check, while its exec ledger had been re-taken.

Pin that the tx-order mint refuses a submitted bound below -1 (#817)

The transition-trace test for a forced order carrying a start bound of -2
assumed such an order could be minted and then judged malformed by the
machine. Since bodies with a bound below -1 no longer decode, the tx-order
mint, which decodes every order's submitted body, refuses them, so no such
order exists for a proof to read. The test is replaced by mint tests that
write the bounds raw into the forced envelope: the sentinel and slot cases
match the encoder byte for byte and are admitted, and a start or end below
-1 is refused.

Document the node's l1_slot_config_mismatch readiness reason

The slot-mapping refusal added with the validRange conversion had no operator text in the readiness reasons doc, so the doc check refused it.

Wait for the phase4 log followers to record before asserting on them

up.sh returns once it has started the four followers, and each records
its docker call a moment later. On a slow runner the up test read only
one follower and a late one wrote into the down test's calls. The up
test now waits for all four before asserting. Also gives the cleanup's
empty catch a comment for no-empty.

Read the derived deployment's slot mapping from the L1 port

A derived-mode deployment (no manifest) needs the L1 slot mapping that the
validRange conversion is parameterised with. It was supplied through a
separate MIDGARD_L1_SLOT_CONFIG setting, a second source of truth that could
disagree with the chain the node actually follows, and which the phase4
bootstrap never set, so a fresh phase4 node refused to start.

Derived mode now reads the mapping through the L1 adapter the role already
holds (follower for node roles, tool adapter for CLI commands); the manifest
path never opens L1. A transient read failure holds startup as
l1_slot_mapping_pending under the bounded startup retry, and a named mismatch
against the deployment stays a non-transient hold. The setting is removed.

Pin the validRange encoding across languages and drop a dead tx-queue hold

A shared hex golden now pins the PlutusV3 and MidgardV1 validRange Data
for finite and absent bounds under one non-trivial slot mapping: the
Aiken derivation and the TypeScript builder must both produce it. A
phase-B test runs an L2 PlutusV3 script that requires a POSIX lower
bound: it passes with the deployment's mapping and fails one slot early
or with a slot-domain context.

The tx-queue processor logged and skipped forever when Lucid had no slot
mapping, with no readiness reason. Startup has already matched the
mapping against the manifest, so that state is a defect, not one to wait
out; it now dies instead of stalling silently.

Regenerate script-hash fixtures for the validity-bound changes

The exclusive upper bound and the decoder's validity-bound check change
the validation machine, the native-tx codec, invalid-range step 01 and
da-hash-preimage step 01, so every script compiling them in has a new
hash. Regenerated through their generators: the two transition-trace fit
ledgers (margins stay positive) and the DA deployment fixture (177
contracts, exactly the scripts that compile those modules). Re-pinned the
contracts registry digest, which covers every applied recipe's hash.

Give L2 Plutus scripts their validity range in POSIX milliseconds

A PlutusV3 script reads txInfoValidRange in POSIX milliseconds, as
Cardano's transValidityInterval builds it. Midgard's L2 script contexts
carried the committed body's raw L1 slots instead, so a script checking a
time bound saw values in the wrong domain, and an absent upper bound was
encoded as NegInf/False rather than PosInf/True.

The context derivation now converts each finite bound on the affine
Shelley anchor, zero_time + (slot - zero_slot) * slot_length: an
inclusive finite lower bound, a strict finite upper bound, and an absent
bound as NegInf or PosInf, both inclusive. The MidgardV1 context uses the
same domain. The conversion happens inside the existing derivation, so
the existing validation-trace proofs cover it.

The slot-to-time mapping is a deploy-time parameter of
cek-context-tx-info, recorded in the deployment manifest as l1SlotConfig:
the named networks use their Shelley constants, a custom network or
devnet its Shelley genesis (system start, slot 0, slot length). The node,
watcher and prover refuse a mapping that differs from the manifest; the
node goes unready with L1_SLOT_CONFIG_MISMATCH instead of crash-looping.
A manifest-less node on a custom network takes MIDGARD_L1_SLOT_CONFIG.
The devnet tooling passes the genesis mapping through.

The transaction spec, technical spec and docs describe the time domain.
Regenerated through their generators: the two transition-trace fit
ledgers and the DA deployment fixture; re-pinned the contracts registry
digest and two event-replay trace hashes (absent-upper encoding).

Refuse validity bounds below -1 when decoding a native body (#817)

A body's validity_interval_start/end is -1 (absent) or a slot, but the
codec decoded any signed integer there. The validation machine called a
bound below -1 malformed while the invalid-range normalization read it as
a real lower bound, so the two disagreed about such a body.

Every body decoder and encoder now refuses a bound below -1, on-chain
(expect_validity_bound in the compact and full-body codecs) and in
TypeScript (asValidityBound in native-body.ts). The da-hash-preimage
inspector guards the same range so it stays total: accepting a leaf with
such a bound is convicted there as a malformed proof source. The tx-order
mint decodes forced sources through the same codec, so no forced leaf can
carry one. With every path decoding first, the machine's and phase-A's
"below -1 is malformed" arms are unreachable and are removed.

The spec, CDDL (validity_bound = -1 / uint), technical spec and docs say
so.

Exec ledgers re-taken: two expect_validity_bound checks per body
encode/decode, about +3.7k mem and +0.89M cpu per body decode.

Closes #817

Split the devnet campaign's definition from its runner

The definition (schema validation, the resume digest and each stage's
command) is pure and now lives in campaign-definition.mjs; campaign.mjs
keeps pinning, the build and blueprint freeze, the receipt and the stage
runner.
